winner.title: Red red

evidence.authenticity: Ghanaian chef author; red palm oil, scotch bonnet, ginger, tomatoes cooked until oil rises, canned mackerel and optional shrimp powder, fried ripe plantain, gari; explains the name comes from the red palm oil. Avocado fan garnish and rosemary are modern touches.
evidence.precision: Metric weights for main ingredients (4 of 17 flagged by read as weighted, but most others have counts/sizes like 3 medium onions, 4 large vine tomatoes, 30 g ginger); sensory cues in all 6 steps (beans tender, onions translucent, oil rises to the surface, plantain golden, 1 cm slices); no temperatures; 'large pot/saucepan' sizes vague.
evidence.testing: BBC Good Food test-kitchen published; bicarb for tender beans and 'oil rises' doneness cue show reasoning, but little explicit why-text.
evidence.photos: No step images in schema (stepImagesInSchema 0); 12 images on page, mostly hero or ads; not confirmed as process photos.
evidence.efficiency: Beans simmer while the sauce cooks, plantain fried at the end and kept warm in oven; times stated 1h25 are realistic apart from overnight soak.
evidence.access: Red palm oil, shrimp powder, gari and scotch bonnet need African/online grocers; palm oil and shrimp powder/gari are noted optional or flagged, but no explicit substitutes.

winner.why: Written by a Ghanaian chef with the full traditional build (palm oil, mackerel, plantain, gari) and doneness cues in every step, which beat African Bites' similar precision but less traditional, plantain-free recipe.

runnerUp.title: Red Red (African Stewed Black-Eyed Peas)

evidence.authenticity: Palm oil, ginger, crayfish, tomatoes; African-run site, but smoked paprika and bouillon are additions and it does not cover the plantain.
evidence.precision: Metric and US weights for 9 ingredients; 4 sensory cues; no pan sizes beyond Dutch oven; time cues given for most steps.
evidence.testing: Rated 4.93 from 64 ratings; has soaking and pressure-cooker options and notes.
evidence.photos: 31 images on page, not confirmed as step photos; none in schema.
evidence.efficiency: Stated total time is a soak-inflated 590 minutes; otherwise straightforward and canned-bean shortcut offered.
evidence.access: Canola oil substitute for palm oil, crayfish optional.

runnerUp.why: Slightly less traditional and no fried plantain component, so it trails BBC Good Food by two points.

notes: BBC recipe includes the plantain, so no separate companion is needed. Other results seen but not read: Jamie Oliver / Zoe Adjonyoh, Honest Food, SBS, Milk Street (non-traditional coconut oil). Winner margin over runner-up is small, and photo scores are unconfirmed (no WebFetch check).
